t: The last sentence of paragraph 7 of section 5136 of the Revised Statutes, as amended (12 U.S.C. 24), is amended by striking the word “or” after the words “International Bank for Reconstruction and Development” and inserting a comma in lieu thereof, and by inserting after the words “the Inter-American Development Bank” the words “or the Asian Development Bank”.

fable.w: This section is a purely technical amendment that adds the Asian Development Bank to a list of institutions in the national banking statute (12 U.S.C. 24). The only possible temptation is the reference to international banks as outside entities, but they are merely named in a list; no outside party is consulted, heard, placed on an advisory body, or given a right to sue over any federal decision.

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute that expands the list of international banks eligible for certain activities. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It merely changes the text of a previous law to include another entity.
qwen_block.s: The last sentence of paragraph 7 of section 5136 of the Revised Statutes, as amended (12 U.S.C. 24), is amended by striking the word “or” after the words “International Bank for Reconstruction and Development” and inserting a comma in lieu thereof, and by inserting after the words “the Inter-American Development Bank” the words “or the Asian Development Bank”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that adds "the Asian Development Bank" to a list in 12 U.S.C. 24. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation duty, rulemaking authority or right to sue. The development banks are named only as entities in a list. They are not consulted on any federal decision, so the definition of participation is not met.
opus.b: **Analysis:** The tempting reading would treat the international development banks named here (World Bank, Inter-American Development Bank, Asian Development Bank) as outside parties taking part in something. That reading fails. The banks are named only as issuers of obligations listed in 12 U.S.C. 24, and the amendment simply adds the Asian Development Bank to that list. No outside party is consulted on, or given any role in, a federal decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section is a technical amendment to a statute, specifically updating a list of international banks. It does not create any mechanism for the federal government to consult with the Asian Development Bank or any other outside party before making a decision. It merely changes the text of the law to include another entity in a list, which is not participation.
qwen_chat.s: The last sentence of paragraph 7 of section 5136 of the Revised Statutes, as amended (12 U.S.C. 24), is amended by striking the word “or” after the words “International Bank for Reconstruction and Development” and inserting a comma in lieu thereof, and by inserting after the words “the Inter-American Development Bank” the words “or the Asian Development Bank”.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that adding the Asian Development Bank to a list of entities implies some form of consultation or partnership with that bank, which is an outside entity. However, the text is purely a technical amendment to a statutory list of authorized activities or entities for a specific legal purpose (likely related to the powers of national banks). It does not establish a process for the federal government to consult with the Asian Development Bank before making a decision, nor does it create an advisory body or public comment period. The amendment simply expands the scope of an existing provision.
